archetype.name: Playoff Team (guard-driven, small-ball)
archetype.definition: A team whose deep, top-graded guard and wing group drives an elite early offense and a turnover-forcing defense. It is held back from contender status by a frontcourt that cannot protect the rim or finish possessions on the glass.

report.headline: Elite guards, a hollow middle, and one blowout flattering the numbers
report.take:
Atlanta opens 2026-27 at 2-1 with a Net Rtg of 15.4, third in the league, and a seventh-place spot on the site's Teams tab. That looks like a leap from a 46-36 team that finished 14th here last year. The shape matches what last season hinted at: the defense jumped to ninth then, and it sits seventh now. The offense, 14th a year ago, is fourth with an ORtg of 122. It is built on perimeter talent. The backcourt and wings both grade A-, and Jalen Johnson ranks second on the small-forward tab while carrying a 29 USG %. Dyson Daniels ranks fourth among shooting guards and Nickeil Alexander-Walker sixth.

The style is coherent. The Hawks take the fourth-highest share of their shots from three, at a 46.3 3PA Rate. They protect the ball, with a TOV % of 12.2 (6th), and they force turnovers at a 17.7 Opp TOV % (4th). That gives them more shots than their opponents before anyone's shooting enters the picture. Alexander-Walker, Wiggins and McCollum have all scored efficiently off the ball, and Daniels' 7.7 BPM is the best on the roster among regulars.

The numbers hide how lopsided the sample is. Three games is almost nothing, and the 128-81 demolition of Charlotte accounts for the entire season margin: the Orlando win and the Houston loss came by matching scores. Strip out that night and this is a team that has traded blows with two opponents. Two other figures are likely to drift. The 30.2 Opp 3P % is well below the league's 34, which is mostly opponents missing. The 15.4 Net Rtg will not survive contact with a full schedule.

The real issue sits in the middle. The frontcourt grades D-, and its five listed players have combined for 0.3 Win Shares. Opponents are shooting 76.7% at the rim, 29th in the league and far above the 66.2 league average. The Hawks also rank 24th in DRB %. Opposing power forwards are scoring well above their norms against them. Atlanta does keep teams out of the paint, ranking 10th in Opp Rim Rate, but what gets there goes in. Expect a good team with a real ceiling on the perimeter and a recurring problem whenever an opponent has size.

strengths.title: Deep, top-graded perimeter rotation
strengths.body: Four guards and Johnson carry the team. Both perimeter groups grade A-, with three players inside the top six of their position tabs. This depth is structural rather than a hot week: the backcourt alone has produced most of the team's Win Shares. Shooting like Wiggins' 74.8 TS % will cool, but the quality of the group is real.

strengths.title: Winning the possession battle
strengths.body: Atlanta rarely gives the ball away and takes it away often. That is a repeatable edge that comes from active guards like Daniels rather than shooting luck. Paired with a top-four 3PA Rate, it turns extra possessions into high-value shots. Both turnover rates should hold up better than the shooting splits.

strengths.title: Offense up a tier from last year
strengths.body: The ORtg of 122 ranks fourth. Last season's offense finished 14th and the one before that 18th. The eFG % is well above the league, driven by volume threes and efficient secondary scorers. Some of this is the Charlotte rout, but the shot profile supports a top-ten offense.

concerns.title: No rim protection, no glass
concerns.body: The frontcourt grades D-, and Okongwu and Landale have negative BPMs and modest finishing. Opponents convert at the rim at a rate among the league's worst, far above Atlanta's own levels in recent seasons. The Hawks also lose the defensive glass. This is a roster-construction problem, not noise, and it will show against big front lines.

concerns.title: One blowout inflating everything
concerns.body: The season differential equals the Charlotte margin, and the other two games split evenly. The 55-win pace and the third-ranked Net Rtg rest on that night and on opponents shooting poorly from three. Both should come down toward a solid-but-not-dominant level.

concerns.title: Power forwards feasting
concerns.body: Opposing power forwards are scoring well above their own averages against Atlanta, the worst mark in the league. That fits a lineup that leans on guards and wings and gets thin minutes from its listed power forwards. Three games is a tiny sample, but it lines up with the rim and rebounding numbers.

trend.note: Three games have produced a close road win, a 128-81 rout and a home loss to Houston. That is a wide swing that says more about matchups than direction. It is far too early to read a trend, but the loss came against the first opponent with an elite frontcourt.

weekAhead.headline: Houston rematch, then a soft middle and two road tests
weekAhead.body:
Five games in eight days, three of them on the road. The week opens in Houston against a 3-0 team that just won in Atlanta and grades A+ at both wings and frontcourt, exactly where the Hawks are weakest. Miami follows at home: winless, 30th on the site, and allowing the league's worst Opp 3P %. That is a natural spot for a high-volume shooting team.

Cleveland brings the league's stingiest rim defense but a 24th-ranked offense and the second-worst turnover rate, which plays into Atlanta's ball-hawking. The road trip to winless New Orleans and then Indiana closes the week. The Pelicans' defense ranks 25th and has been shredded by centers. Reasonable expectation is three wins, with the Houston rematch the hardest game to bank.

keyMatchups.title: Hawks' size problem vs Houston
keyMatchups.body: Houston's frontcourt grades A+ against Atlanta's D-, and the Rockets already won the first meeting 121-114. Their defense has been generous to small forwards, which is where Johnson operates. Atlanta's path is Johnson attacking while the guards force turnovers to offset the size gap.

keyMatchups.title: Threes against Miami's leaky perimeter
keyMatchups.body: Miami ranks last in Opp 3P % and has given up big nights to shooting guards. Atlanta's guard-heavy, three-heavy attack lines up perfectly. This is the week's clearest win if the Hawks avoid a letdown.

keyMatchups.title: A rare chance for Atlanta's bigs
keyMatchups.body: New Orleans has allowed the most points to centers in the league. That is an opening for Okongwu and Landale to contribute offensively after a quiet start. The flip side is a Pelicans frontcourt graded A, which will test Atlanta's rim defense.

weekAhead.watch: Whether opponents' shooting at the rim comes down at all. Facing Houston's and New Orleans' frontcourts, it decides whether this defense is top-ten or a mirage.

restOfSeason.body:
The perimeter core is good enough to keep Atlanta comfortably in the East's playoff picture, and the turnover edge and shot profile should travel. Two things will regress. The Net Rtg will come down as the Charlotte rout fades into a bigger sample, and the 30.2 Opp 3P % will drift toward the league's 34. The 55-win pace is the ceiling of the picture, not the forecast. A team that kept last season's defensive gains and added a top-ten offense projects to roughly 45 to 52 wins, with a Net Rtg around +2 to +6.

The frontcourt is what separates that range from the top of the East. If the rim defense and defensive glass merely reach league-average, the defense can stay top-ten. If not, bigger opponents will keep exposing it, as Houston did.
swingFactors: Frontcourt rim protection and defensive rebounding
Johnson's efficiency at a heavy usage load

confidence.note: Three games, one of them a 128-81 outlier.
